name: tsa_restaurantLogin
description: Restaurant portal login: returns the active restaurant whose plain-text shared passphrase (TSA.Restaurant.portalPassword) equals @password, or zero rows. Low-stakes internal tool by design. portalPassword was added by db/hc6/tsa/archive/add_restaurant_portal_password.sql and is missing from db/schema/tables/TSA.Restaurant.Table.sql. Called by the TSA Eats Next.js app (tsa-eats/lib/api.ts) through api/Endpoints/TsaApi.cs, which maps queryType 'restaurantLogin' to [TSA].[tsa_restaurantLogin]. There is no Harrier Central auth: POST requires the shared X-Api-Key (TsaApiKey); GET requires nothing, and the shim does not restrict which procedure a GET may name. The shim turns any one-row rowset with Success = 0 into HTTP 400 {success:false, errorMessage}, and an empty first rowset into HTTP 404.

parameters.name: password
parameters.description: Passphrase entered on the login page. No default.

codeSmells.detail: @password (line 2) have no SQL default. A caller that omits one is refused by SQL Server before the body runs: no log row, and the TsaApi shim returns a generic 500.

codeSmells.issue: SP body not wrapped in TRY/CATCH
codeSmells.detail: Read procedure with no TRY/CATCH: any runtime error (timeout, deadlock) becomes an unlogged raw 500 from the shim.

codeSmells.issue: Plain-text passwords, brute-forceable without a key
codeSmells.detail: Passphrases are stored and compared in plain text (line 21), and the shim's GET route lets anyone try passwords with no X-Api-Key and no rate limit.
Lines 17-22: two restaurants sharing a passphrase log in as an arbitrary one.
db/schema/tables/TSA.Restaurant.Table.sql does not declare portalPassword NVARCHAR(100) NULL, which this SP reads.

breakingChangeRules: Never remove a column from any rowset
Never change a sentinel value meaning
Never change errorType integer codes without updating all callers
